moments.reason: Reuters asks the headline question; NASA confirms meteoroid finding and no Crew-6 impact.
The reveal: hole in radiator AND coolant pipe, crew extension of months. Money quotes.
Evacuation scenario Q&A — the tense 'what if' every viewer wonders.
Forensics: they fired a high-velocity gun at an aluminum plate; a ~1mm particle at ~7km/s caused it.
Crew staying ~a year; their reaction + SpaceX backup + the ice-cream joke — human moment.
Why a crewed landing is risky: no heat rejection → high temp in equipment/crew compartments.
Specifics: Soyuz computer hits high-30s C; 'in an area that would be not healthy for the crew.'
Redundancy plan: analog-equipment fallback; humidity is the real crew killer.
SpaceX contingency detail: crew straps in where cargo flies; one crew member minimum.
'Space is not safe place' — the scenario was rehearsed before they ever flew. Quotable.
The framing moment: 'I'm not calling it a rescue Soyuz... it's a replacement Soyuz.'
Micrometeoroid vs space junk: velocity physics + visible strike marks on windows.
Why no in-space repair: far end, no handrails, coolant refill is riskier than replacement.
The shielding defense: radiator must face open space; no shield stops a 7 km/s bullet.
Concrete contingency: crew strapped into Dragon's cargo area with Soyuz hardware.
